title: Maintaining the Finished Application knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Maintaining the Finished Application”?
options: Maintaining the Finished Application means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Maintaining the Finished Application removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Maintaining the Finished Application should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Maintaining the Finished Application helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Maintaining the Finished Application helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Maintaining the Finished Application is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Handling bug reports” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Handling bug reports” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Handling bug reports” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Handling bug reports” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Handling bug reports” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Handling bug reports” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Handling bug reports” under Maintaining the Finished Application. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Maintaining the Finished Application”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
